verdicts.strongest_argument: Every factual component of this claim is in the captured wire copy, and the two anchors the hunter uses for magnitude are published company guidance. The $70-80bn SPV financing is the headline 'Broadcom (AVGO) Nears $70B Debt Financing Deal, Sources Say' on Yahoo Finance, dated 2026-08-21 and indexed as `new` in snapshots/20260831T152242Z.json (sha 5cd36372...) with the story recurring in the 08-30 and 09-01 sweeps too - this is top-of-feed coverage on a $1.77tn market cap, not an obscure trade note. The $35bn Anthropic compute commitment was 'unveiled in June' by the hunter's own description; the '$30bn AI bookings and backlog' and '$60bn cumulative' figures are, again by the hunter's own words, what 'the pre-print preview coverage in this same corpus anchors readers on'; and Hock Tan's '~$19bn H1, double it in H2' is a direct quote from the Q2 FY26 earnings call transcript, i.e. guidance already given to the whole market on 2026-06-03. That is the 90-100 band by definition. The residual novelty is a reframe - read the lease paper as a forward booking indicator rather than as credit risk - which is analysis, not information, and the hunter concedes the market saw the item and moved ~1% on it. The absence of an 8-K or S-3 confirming the financing does not make the story unpriced; it makes it a sourced press report, which is exactly how such deals trade, and the corpus itself shows the report circulating for twelve days before the print. Finally, the hunter's tape argument is backwards: the -12.2% 20-day drawdown is not the market failing to connect the financing, because the drawdown happened on 08-18/08-19 (392.43 -> 362.48, -7.6% on 35.1m shares vs a 20.2m 20d average), *before* the 08-21 report, after which the stock actually rose to 368.45 and then recovered to ~370 into the print. I hold back the last 12 points because nothing in the capture sizes the FY26 Q4 AI revenue number the financing would imply, so the specific magnitude of a backlog disclosure at this print is genuinely undrawn.
